patient.name: Connor Whitfield
patient.chiefComplaint: Right shoulder pain and deformity after a rugby collision

history.hpi: Patient was tackled during a rugby match and landed on an outstretched right arm. He immediately felt his shoulder "pop out" and has been unable to move it since. Reports severe pain rated 9/10, worse with any attempted movement. Denies numbness initially but now reports mild tingling in the fingertips.
history.lastOralIntake: Sports drink and a banana approximately 1 hour prior to injury
history.events: Teammates called 911 immediately after the collision; patient has been seated on the sideline holding his arm since

scene.dispatch: 22-year-old male, injury, rugby field, arm injury
scene.location: Outdoor rugby field, patient seated on the sideline supported by teammates
scene.safety: No hazards to crew; game paused, teammates and coach present
scene.bystanders: Teammates and coach present, witnessed the collision, called 911 immediately
visualCues: Patient seated, holding right arm against his body with left hand
Visible squaring/loss of normal shoulder contour on the right
Patient guarding the arm, resistant to any movement
No open wounds or active bleeding
Right hand fingertips slightly pale compared to left

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 22-year-old male seated on the sideline, holding his right arm, with an obviously deformed right shoulder following a rugby collision.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse present and strong bilaterally, mild pallor to right fingertips
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Unable to move right shoulder/arm due to pain; grip strength intact but painful; left arm fully intact
otherFindings: Right shoulder 9/10 pain, worse with any movement
Squared-off deformity to right shoulder contour
Mild tingling reported in right fingertips
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It's killing me, please don't touch it — my fingers feel kind of tingly too."

transitions.condition: Crew assesses distal pulse/sensation/motor function of the right arm, splints the shoulder in position found, and administers weight-based IV morphine with vital sign monitoring.

phases.name: Neurovascular assessed, splinted, pain treated
phases.description: Crew completes a focused assessment of the extremity, confirms distal pulse/sensation/movement, splints the shoulder in the position found, and administers IV morphine dosed to the patient's weight while monitoring vital signs for respiratory depression or hypotension.
phases.triggerCondition: After confirming no other injuries on primary survey, the crew recognizes the shoulder deformity as a suspected dislocation, assesses neurovascular status, splints the extremity, and treats the patient's severe pain with weight-based IV morphine per protocol.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial and distal pulses present bilaterally, fingertip color improving
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation intact to light touch, distal pulses strong; unable to actively move shoulder due to splinting
otherFindings: Right shoulder splinted in position found
No new neurovascular deficits after splinting
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That's already helping a lot, thank you."

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess distal pulse, sensation, and movement of right arm before splinting
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Vascular status of extremity: Pallor, Pulse, Capillary refill and skin temperature. Neurologic status of extremity: Sensation to light touch, Distal movement of extremity
expectedActions.rationale: Establishes a neurovascular baseline before splinting to detect vascular or nerve compromise from the dislocation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess pain using Numeric Rating Scale (patient is 22 years old)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Greater than 12 years old: Self-report scale: Numeric Rating Scale (NRS)
expectedActions.rationale: Establishes a baseline pain score to guide dosing and document response to treatment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Morphine 8 mg IV (82 kg × 0.1 mg/kg = 8.2 mg, rounded to 8 mg; max initial dose 10 mg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For Moderate to Severe pain, analgesics include: Morphine sulfate: 0.1 mg/kg IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose is 10 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Weight-based opioid dosing for severe (9/10) pain from an acute dislocation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Splint shoulder/arm in position found; do not force reduction
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Use splints as appropriate to limit movement of suspected fracture
expectedActions.rationale: Immobilizing in the position found limits further pain and soft tissue injury without attempting field reduction.

expectedActions.shortAction: Monitor SpO2 and respiratory rate closely after morphine for signs of hypoventilation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Use of non-invasive capnography is an earlier predictor of hypoventilation than pulse oximetry if opioid medications are administered
expectedActions.rationale: Opioids carry a respiratory depression risk requiring close post-dose monitoring.

transitions.if: Pain reassessed, BP stable, ready for transport
transitions.condition: Pain score has decreased, vital signs remain stable with no signs of hypotension or respiratory depression, and the extremity is splinted for transport.
Crew administers the weight-based morphine dose but fails to reassess blood pressure afterward, missing the onset of opioid-related hypotension.

phases.name: Pain reassessed, BP stable, ready for transport
phases.description: Patient is splinted, pain is improving, and vital signs remain stable. Crew transports in a position of comfort with continued reassessment.
phases.triggerCondition: After morphine administration and splinting, the crew reassesses pain score and vital signs, confirms hemodynamic stability, and prepares the patient for transport.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial and distal pulses strong bilaterally

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess pain score and vital signs after morphine administration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Pain severity scores should be recorded before and after analgesic medication administration and upon arrival at destination
expectedActions.rationale: Documents medication effectiveness and supports the decision on whether repeat dosing is needed.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport in position of comfort with continued reassessment
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Transport in position of comfort and reassess as indicated
expectedActions.rationale: Minimizes ongoing pain and monitors for delayed medication effects en route.

phases.name: Morphine given without BP reassessment
phases.description: The crew administered morphine but did not reassess blood pressure or respiratory status afterward. The patient becomes hypotensive and mildly drowsy, an under-recognized opioid effect that a timely reassessment would have caught.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew fails to reassess vital signs after morphine administration, missing early evidence of opioid-related hypotension and mild sedation.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and distal pulses intact but patient is drowsy and slow to respond
otherFindings: Patient more drowsy than expected for dose given
Blood pressure not reassessed since morphine administration

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize opioid-related hypotension/sedation; reassess vitals and titrate care
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer opioids with caution to patients with Glasgow Coma Score (GCS) less than 15, hypotension, identified medication allergy, hypoxia (SPO2 less than 90%) after maximal supplemental oxygen therapy, or signs of hypoventilation
expectedActions.rationale: Delayed recognition of opioid-related hypotension and sedation risks further deterioration en route.
